glomeris autopilot — Read, grant or revoke a bounded standing authorization.

usage: glomeris autopilot <show|enable|revoke|run> [--kinds <tag,...>]
                [--max-actions <N>] [--max-bytes <N>] [--max-duration <secs>]
                [--min-pressure <state|none>]
                [--preauthorize-ask <kind>:<reason>] [--json] [--dry-run]
                [--plan-file <path>] [--project-root <path>]...

Safety depends on the subcommand; each is labelled below. The strongest of
them: Can delete data — every deletion is policy-gated.

A standing grant with limits, written down where you can read it. Only `run`
can delete anything, and only what the grant already allowed: an envelope
authorizes resource kinds, a number of actions, a byte total, a wall-clock
budget and optionally a disk-pressure floor, and every candidate is still
classified by policy and revalidated immediately before deletion.

Defaults grant nothing: with no envelope file, Autopilot is revoked and `run`
executes nothing. AUTO_SAFE resources are the only ones a grant reaches by
default; PROTECTED refuses unconditionally and no flag here can change that;
ASK refuses unless that exact kind and reason were pre-authorized.

An LLM's only possible influence is --plan-file, which reorders candidates
this machine already found. It cannot add a candidate, choose an action,
supply a path, or raise a limit. There is no live-provider mode: asking a
model is `llm-plan`'s job, so no deletion here waits on a network call.

Subcommands
  show [--json]
      Read-only — changes nothing.
      Print the stored envelope and where it lives. The default, so a bare
      `glomeris autopilot` reads rather than acts.
  enable
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Write a new envelope from the flags on this command line and turn
      Autopilot on. Requires --kinds. Replaces the previous envelope
      rather than adding to it, so one line states the whole grant.
  revoke
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Turn Autopilot off. Takes effect on the next run — every run
      re-reads the file, so there is nothing to restart. Limits are kept
      so a later enable cannot return with limits you never read.
  run
      Can delete data — every deletion is policy-gated.
      Consider the discovered candidates within the envelope. Without
      --dry-run this deletes. Holds the execution lock, so it exits 75 if
      another invocation already holds it.

Options
  --kinds <tag,...>
      For `enable`: the resource kinds the grant covers, by the tags
      `actions list` prints, comma-separated. `unknown` is refused.
  --max-actions <N>
      For `enable`: how many actions one run may perform. Defaults to 3
      and cannot exceed 25.
  --max-bytes <N>
      For `enable`: the byte total one run may reclaim. Defaults to 5 GiB
      and cannot exceed 64 GiB.
  --max-duration <secs>
      For `enable`: the wall-clock budget for one run, in whole seconds.
      Defaults to 60 and cannot exceed 900.
  --min-pressure <state|none>
      For `enable`: refuse to run unless disk pressure is at least this
      state. `none` (the default) does not require any. Unobservable
      pressure fails any floor you set.
  --preauthorize-ask <kind>:<reason>
      For `enable`: narrowly authorize one ASK reason for one kind, e.g.
      node_modules:rebuild_cost_high. Repeatable. Every PROTECTED reason
      and every evidence-quality reason is refused here, so this cannot
      become a blanket consent.
  --json
      For `show`, `enable` and `revoke`: print the envelope as JSON —
      the grant, the hard ceilings, every choice `enable` would accept,
      and what no envelope can ever authorize. The same shape from all
      three, always describing what is in force after the command ran.
      This is what the menu-bar app reads.
  --dry-run
      For `run`: show the real bounded plan, including where a budget cuts
      it off, and delete nothing.
  --plan-file <path>
      For `run`: read an LLM plan (see `llm-plan --schema`) and use it to
      order candidates. Ordering is its entire authority.
  --project-root <path>
      Same meaning as for `detect`. Repeatable.

Examples
  glomeris autopilot
      What is Autopilot allowed to do right now?
  glomeris autopilot enable --kinds node_modules \
    --max-actions 1 --max-bytes 1073741824
      Grant one narrow thing, and nothing else.
  glomeris autopilot run --dry-run
      What would it do, before letting it do anything?
  glomeris autopilot revoke
      Stop it, now.

Exit codes
  0   the run finished inside its envelope, including when it found
      nothing it was allowed to do.
  1   an action executed and failed, or the envelope file could not be
      read or written.
  2   usage error, including an unknown resource kind, a limit above its
      ceiling, or `enable` without --kinds.
  3   Autopilot is not enabled, so nothing was attempted.
  75  another glomeris invocation holds the execution lock.
  Run `glomeris help exit-codes` for the codes shared by every command.

See also: execute, free, llm-plan, actions
